overall: The AG found the Fitchburg Board of Health did not violate the Open Meeting Law in the March 3 public-comment complaint, because the Chair may set participation rules and the Board may reorder topics. The gender discrimination claim was declined as outside the statute.

allegations.summary: Alleged the Board delayed public comment at its March 3 meeting by hearing the Superintendent and voting on orders before taking public comment.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, the Law does not prohibit a public body from removing, postponing, or declining to discuss a topic listed on a meeting notice or taking topics in a different order than listed on the notice, as the Board did here when it heard from the Superintendent before the public.

allegations.summary: Alleged the Board limited public participation at the March 3 meeting, including by taking public comment only after voting on the orders.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require that a public body allow public participation in its meetings, but rather provides that “[n]o person shall address a meeting of a public body without permission of the chair, and all persons shall, at the request of the chair, be silent.”

allegations.summary: Alleged that the Board engaged in gender discrimination; the AG's Division of Open Government declined to review this non-Open Meeting Law claim.
allegations.key_passage: Even if true, this allegation would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law, and therefore we decline to review it.
